teaching_contrasts.now: One retrieval route can contain transactions involving candidate committees, PAC-style objects, party-style objects, and issue or referendum objects.
teaching_contrasts.why: Sharing a route does not make the political objects equivalent.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Route membership may support comparison, but it may not silently infer object kind, candidate status, office, or authority.

teaching_contrasts.now: A bounded practice source can narrow geography while live jurisdiction selectors remain unavailable.
teaching_contrasts.why: A simulated retrieval aperture must not appear combinable with live custodians or imply those custodians were queried.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Practice may narrow the aperture to a declared fictional jurisdiction, but live geography remains inert until exit and no live source may be consulted from that route.

teaching_contrasts.now: One contributor may appear with a formal or familiar name, a missing middle initial, or more than one legitimate address while remaining one review candidate.
teaching_contrasts.why: Identity continuity can survive surface-field variation, but similarity alone cannot close identity.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Declared alias and compatible-middle evidence may support one candidate cluster; address, employer, and name variation remain visible and human closure remains required.

teaching_contrasts.now: Different contributors may share an address, employer, city, state, or postal field.
teaching_contrasts.why: A corroborating field can strengthen a comparison without becoming an identity key.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Shared fields may raise candidate similarity but may never automatically merge contributors or erase contradictory identity evidence.

teaching_contrasts.now: Two filing rows can describe successive versions of one underlying transaction rather than two independent transactions.
teaching_contrasts.why: Naive summation and naive deduplication can both destroy filing history.
teaching_contrasts.exact: A declared revision relationship must remain visible until an operator decides how the transaction should be interpreted; revision order cannot be silently flattened.

teaching_contrasts.now: The same name can appear as a contributor identity and as part of a candidate or committee identity.
teaching_contrasts.why: Lexical identity does not collapse donor role into political-object role.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Route role remains first-class: contributor, candidate, committee, organization, and filer projections may share names while remaining non-equivalent objects.

teaching_contrasts.now: A discovered name can be carried into another search surface without starting that search.
teaching_contrasts.why: Preserving discovery context should reduce operator burden without stealing the next retrieval gesture.
teaching_contrasts.exact: A handoff may prepare a query and preserve route provenance, but it may not alter search semantics or begin retrieval until the operator explicitly acts.

teaching_contrasts.now: Otherwise different contributor histories can suddenly converge on the same dates, political objects, and unusually large transaction magnitudes.
teaching_contrasts.why: An episodic pattern can become investigatively salient precisely because the longer histories remain distinct.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Repeated co-temporality and magnitude spikes may be surfaced as patterns for review, but coordination, common control, common identity, or causation may not be inferred automatically.

teaching_contrasts.now: Most contribution records can remain visually quiet while a small minority carry a meaningful transaction class such as loan or in-kind.
teaching_contrasts.why: A sparse but consequential source field should become visible when it changes how a transaction must be interpreted.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Transaction class may be promoted from source semantics without discarding the original source type; ordinary cash records remain unbadged.

teaching_contrasts.now: A source-observed value can conflict with an expected limit or rule.
teaching_contrasts.why: Automatically repairing the value can erase the exact anomaly that deserves review.
teaching_contrasts.exact: When a declared practice anomaly is present, preserve the observed value, surface the review condition, and forbid silent normalization from converting the record into a compliant one.

teaching_contrasts.now: A contributor cluster may repeatedly support some political objects while showing no observed transactions to another object in the available aperture.
teaching_contrasts.why: Absence within an observed record set can become a useful comparison without becoming proof of hostility, opposition, or intent.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Negative-space patterns may be surfaced as hypotheses for further retrieval, but absence may not be converted into a positive claim about motive or allegiance.

teaching_contrasts.now: The same actor can recur across different races, committees, cycles, and transaction dates, while some cross-object dates coincide and others remain separated.
teaching_contrasts.why: Actor continuity and timing patterns help trace a history, but neither a repeated name nor co-temporality makes distinct political episodes equivalent.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Preserve actor identity, race or committee episode, cycle, and source date separately. Surface repeated or coincident patterns for review; never infer common control, transfer, coordination, causation, or episode equivalence automatically.
